brief_rationale: This trajectory spans 23 turns across a preoperative-admission-through-discharge episode. The doctor proactively tracks staged results, screens for blocking symptoms, provides doxazosin safety instructions, and establishes an executable team-contact plan. No serious responsibility-chain error is present; all seven RCs are met or partially met with no minor/moderate error in the six major RCs. However, RC7 (receipt/teach-back closure) is only partially completed: the patient confirms understanding of individual plan components across turns, but the final closure turn does not contain a single, comprehensive confirmation of all plan elements, which constitutes a minor omission. Several high-order points are triggered and actively completed with meaningful impact, notably HO1 (reprioritization when CT returned and later when admission logistics surfaced), HO2 (verification of ambiguous app/phone-based report statuses), HO3 (real-world constraint navigation plan with checklist, channels, and caregiver role), and HO4 (correction of misconceptions about anesthesia review, pending status, and doxazosin self-management). The closure is safe, executable, traceable, and valid_open (handoff to surgical/anesthesia team with patient carrying materials). The minor RC7 defect prevents a perfect grade; the trajectory satisfies Strong (Grade 4) with one minor error and at least one completed high-order point.
